conventions.convention: AdaBoost starts with uniform weights and zero score, uses half-log coefficients, returns the perfect base classifier when weighted error is zero, and reports weak-learning failure when weighted error is at least 1/2. Score ties predict +1.
The empirical score loss is a sum, without a 1/N factor; pseudo-residuals are negative derivatives with respect to individual scores.

Gradient boosting uses full-sample finite-depth CART to determine regions, then updates with exact leafwise loss-minimizing offsets rather than fitted residual means. Initial and leafwise minima must be attained.
The AdaBoost bound concerns completed rounds with 0 < e_m < 1/2, includes nonpositive margins, and assigns the empty product value 1 at M = 0.

load_bearing.statement: On an admitted finite run, initialize with an attained constant loss minimizer, fit finite-depth CART to negative score derivatives, choose an attained real loss-minimizing offset separately in each terminal leaf, and add those offsets to the current score.

Initialize w_i = 1/N and F_0 = 0. For 0 < e_m < 1/2 use a_m = (1/2) log((1-e_m)/e_m), Z_m = 2√(e_m(1-e_m)), normalized exponential weight updates, and additive score updates; handle zero error and weak-learning failure separately.

For scalar losses differentiable at the sample scores in an open scalar domain U, the finite sum Φ on U^N is totally differentiable, DΦ(z)v = Σ_i ∂₂ℓ(y_i,z_i)v_i, and the pseudo-residual vector equals −∇Φ(z).

For any finite sequence of completed AdaBoost rounds with 0 < e_m < 1/2, Σ_i exp(−y_iF_M(x_i)) = N∏_m Z_m, and the nonpositive-margin fraction, hence empirical classification error under the +1 tie rule, is at most ∏_m Z_m.
For a finite sample and scalar losses differentiable at the current scores, r_i(f) = −dℓ(y_i,t)/dt evaluated at t = f(x_i), with empirical score loss Φ(z) = Σ_i ℓ(y_i,z_i).

seams_checked.note: Checked the CART page and actual empirical-tree definition, leaf-mean theorem, growth algorithm, and termination theorem against the boosting consumers. CART supplies a finite-depth regression fit with nonempty terminal sample sets partitioning the sample, including a single root leaf at depth zero. Boosting uses its residual means for fitting regions and separately computes exact loss-minimizing update offsets. The loss theorem uses only the finite partition and attained leafwise minima; no global tree optimality or strict-descent guarantee is imported.
